record.original_question: Let M_S be the spherical maximal operator on R^d, defined by taking at each x the supremum over r > 0 of the average of |f| on the sphere S^{d-1}(x,r). For dimensions d >= 2, is M_S bounded as an operator from W^{1,p}(R^d) to W^{1,p}(R^d) throughout the full endpoint range 1 < p <= d/(d-1)?

evidence.quote: In the scope of Theorem 2.2, one may consider the spherical maximal operator. Letting S d−1 (x, r) ⊂ Rd be the (d − 1)-dimensional sphere of center x and radius r, this operator is defined as MS f (x) = sup_{r>0} 1/(ω_{d−1} r^{d−1}) ∫_{S^{d−1}(x,r)} |f(z)| dσ(z).
Question 5. Let d ≥ 2. Is MS : W 1,p (Rd) → W 1,p (Rd) bounded for 1 < p ≤ d/(d − 1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d\ge 2$, let $S^{d-1}(x,r)=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^d:|z-x|=r\}$ denote the $(d-1)$-dimensional sphere of center $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and radius $r>0$, equipped with its surface measure $\sigma$, and let $\omega_{d-1}$ denote the surface area of the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The spherical maximal operator $M_S$ is defined for locally integrable $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ by
$$M_S f(x)=\sup_{r>0}\frac{1}{\omega_{d-1} r^{d-1}}\int_{S^{d-1}(x,r)}|f(z)|\,d\sigma(z).$$
For $1<p<\infty$, the Sobolev space $W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ consists of those $f\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ whose distributional gradient $\nabla f$ also lies in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, with norm $\|f\|_{W^{1,p}}=\|f\|_{L^p}+\|\nabla f\|_{L^p}$.

Question: For every $d\ge 2$ and every $p$ with $1<p\le d/(d-1)$, is $M_S$ a bounded operator from $W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^d)$?

artifact.status_search_result: Available sources indicate that boundedness of the spherical maximal operator on $\dot W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ has been established for $d/(d-1)<p<\infty$ (with appropriate dimensional restrictions), and the endpoint $p=d/(d-1)$ together with the range $1<p<d/(d-1)$ is reported as an open problem. Recent work on related (e.g., strong) spherical maximal operators continues but does not appear to resolve this endpoint Sobolev question.
